overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance metrics highlights a dominant viewer preference for space and cosmic 'What If' scenarios, particularly extreme planetary environments and counter-intuitive physical phenomena. Videos focused on unusual planetary conditions (e.g., liquid diamond planets, burning ice, dark planets) generate the highest view counts and engagement rates (likes-per-view). Psychological and biological trivia underperforms compared to high-concept cosmic scale and visual curiosity hooks.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views) outperform standard fact formats by coupling hypothetical extreme survival with dazzling cosmic visuals.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more high-stakes cosmic 'What If' scenarios focusing on surreal planetary environments.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles featuring bizarre planetary phenomena such as 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,030 views) and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (725 views) drive high view velocity.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on bizarre celestial weather and extreme exoplanet anomalies with strong visual contrast.

weak_patterns.pattern: Abstract Psychological Trivia Without Visual Stakes
weak_patterns.evidence: Content like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories 🤯' (5 views) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head 🧠' (17 views) show significantly lower viewer retention and engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize abstract internal psychology facts unless they feature an extreme, counter-intuitive visual or physical experiment.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos such as 'The 2,000-Year-Old Mystery Science Can't Solve' (139 views) underperform relative to high-concept space and universe-scale content.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot away from standard historical artifact mysteries toward futuristic, space, or deep-earth geographic phenomena.

next_video.concept: What Happens If You Stepped Onto a Rogue Planet Wandering Through Interstellar Space?
next_video.opening_direction: Start with total pitch blackness and absolute zero temperature, asking the viewer what happens when a world has no sun.
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that hundreds of billions of rogue planets drift invisibly between stars in our galaxy alone, completely untethered from any solar system.
next_video.reason: Capitalizes on the proven high performance of extreme planetary immersion and dark/cold space concepts (e.g., TrES-2b and burning ice planets), while introducing an entirely fresh celestial phenomenon.
fresh_topic_constraints: Must not feature diamond planets, liquid metal rain, or previously used exoplanets like TrES-2b.
Focus exclusively on rogue planets and interstellar space drift.

experiment: Test a 21-second space survival scenario focusing on an invisible rogue planet to see if the combination of absolute darkness and cosmic isolation matches or exceeds the engagement rate of diamond/ice planet videos.
